label: Appearance
value: Anne is a tall woman.
unit: Anne is a tall, slender woman with a milk-white, freckled complexion, luminous gray eyes that appear green in some lights, and thick hair that darkened from plain red in her youth to a rich auburn. She has a broad forehead, a pronounced pointed chin, a shapely nose, and an expressive mouth that curves into a sweet smile. Her face is constantly illuminated by her ever-varying emotions and vivid imagination.

value: Anne is intensely imaginative.
unit: Anne is an intensely imaginative, passionate, and romantic individual who experiences life's joys and sorrows with heightened intensity. She is fiercely loyal, generous, and affectionate toward her friends, possessing a natural warmth that wins over people of all ages. Though she can be impulsive, quick-tempered, and stubborn when her pride or sense of justice is stirred, she is deeply conscientious, introspective, and quick to repent her mistakes. She finds profound joy in the beauty of nature, poetry, and kindred spirits, maintaining a youthful enthusiasm and optimism even amid heartbreak and disappointment.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables
unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, due to a mistake when Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert sent for an orphan boy. Though Marilla initially intended to send her back, Matthew's fond desire and Anne's passionate plea won her a home at Green Gables. She quickly made a bosom friend in Diana Barry, but her early years in Avonlea were filled with misadventures—losing her temper at Mrs. Rachel Lynde, accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine, dyeing her hair green, and breaking her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head when he called her 'Carrots.' After a rivalry in school, Anne attended Queen's Academy, winning the Avery Scholarship. Upon Matthew's sudden death, she gave up college to stay at Green Gables with Marilla and taught the Avonlea school for two years, during which she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helped care for the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. After Mrs. Lynde moved in with Marilla, Anne attended Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in English. During college she refused proposals from Billy Andrews, Charlie Sloane, and the wealthy Roy Gardner, eventually realizing her deep love for her longtime rival and friend, Gilbert Blythe. After teaching three years as principal of Summerside High School, she married Gilbert in the Green Gables orchard and moved to a little 'house of dreams' in Four Winds Harbor. There she suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn baby, Joyce, before giving birth to a healthy son, James Matthew.

unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, due to a mistake when Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert sent for an orphan boy. Though Marilla initially intended to send her back, Matthew's fond desire and Anne's passionate plea won her a home at Green Gables. She quickly made a bosom friend in Diana Barry, but her early years in Avonlea were filled with misadventures—losing her temper at Mrs. Rachel Lynde, accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine, dyeing her hair green, and breaking her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head when he called her 'Carrots.' After a rivalry in school, Anne attended Queen's Academy, winning the Avery Scholarship. Upon Matthew's sudden death, she gave up college to stay at Green Gables with Marilla and taught the Avonlea school for two years, during which she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helped care for the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. After Mrs. Lynde moved in with Marilla, Anne attended Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in English. During college she refused proposals from Billy Andrews, Charlie Sloane, and the wealthy Roy Gardner, eventually realizing her deep love for her longtime rival and friend, Gilbert Blythe. After teaching three years as principal of Summerside High School, she married Gilbert in the Green Gables orchard and moved to a little 'house of dreams' in Four Winds Harbor. There she suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn baby, Joyce, before giving birth to a healthy son, James Matthew.

She quickly made a bosom friend in Diana Barry, but her early years in Avonlea were filled with misadventures—losing her temper at Mrs. Rachel Lynde, accidentally intoxicating Diana with currant wine, dyeing her hair green, and breaking her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head when he called her 'Carrots.' After a rivalry in school, Anne attended Queen's Academy, winning the Avery Scholarship. Upon Matthew's sudden death, she gave up college to stay at Green Gables with Marilla and taught the Avonlea school for two years, during which she founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helped care for the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. After Mrs. Lynde moved in with Marilla, Anne attended Redmond College in Kingsport, graduating with High Honors in English. During college she refused proposals from Billy Andrews, Charlie Sloane, and the wealthy Roy Gardner, eventually realizing her deep love for her longtime rival and friend, Gilbert Blythe. After teaching three years as principal of Summerside High School, she married Gilbert in the Green Gables orchard and moved to a little 'house of dreams' in Four Winds Harbor. There she suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn baby, Joyce, before giving birth to a healthy son, James Matthew.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye came to live in Avonlea.
unit: Anthony Pye came to live in Avonlea after being taken in as an orphan nephew by Mr. and Mrs. George Pye. When Anne Shirley began her teaching career at the Avonlea school, Anthony was one of her new pupils and immediately displayed a sullen, defiant attitude toward her because she was a girl. He engaged in various pranks, including mocking Anne, making rude remarks about her hair, and dropping a mouse into her desk drawer. After the mouse incident, Anne lost her temper and gave him a whipping with her pointer. Contrary to her fears, the whipping earned Anthony's respect, and the next day he offered to carry her books and began behaving much better in school. When Anne resigned two years later to attend college, Anthony was so upset that he fought two pitched battles with other boys to vent his feelings, ultimately declaring that Anne was a good teacher after all.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina lived alone in a large house
unit: Aunt Jamesina lived alone in a large house after her only daughter, Elizabeth, married and left for a foreign mission field in India. Being lonely, she accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport and act as housekeeper and chaperone for her niece Stella Maynard and her friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and later adopted Rusty as well. Aunt Jamesina kept house for the girls during their remaining two years at Redmond College, offering them homely wisdom, cheerful company, and motherly care. When the girls graduated and Patty's Place was returned to its owners, Aunt Jamesina chose to remain in Kingsport or return home, taking all three cats with her to Green Gables before heading back.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea as part of the large Andrews connection. During his youth he attended local events, including driving Anne Shirley, Jane Andrews, and Diana Barry to a concert at the White Sands Hotel, where his extreme shyness kept him mostly silent. He held a long-standing admiration for Anne Shirley, and when his father offered to deed him the family's upper farm upon his marriage, he attempted to propose to her. Too timid to speak for himself, he enlisted his sister Jane to propose to Anne on his behalf. After Anne rejected the proposal, Billy turned his attentions to Nettie Blewett, whom he married the following year. The couple subsequently 'appeared out' together at the Avonlea church to the great pride of the Andrews family.

label: History
value: Captain Jim spent his youth in Four Winds.
unit: Captain Jim spent his youth in Four Winds, where he befriended John Selwyn, the local schoolmaster, and witnessed the arrival of Selwyn's bride to their new home on the harbor shore. In his teens he ran away to sea, spending decades sailing the globe and experiencing shipwreck, mutiny, marooning, and battles. In his youth he loved a girl named Margaret, but she tragically drowned in a summer squall, an event that left an enduring mark on his life. Years later, while in Havana, he discovered an amnesiac sailor whom he believed to be Dick Moore, bringing him back to his wife Leslie. Retiring from the sea, Captain Jim became the keeper of the Four Winds Light, living a quiet life accompanied by his cat, the First Mate. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved into the old Selwyn house, he instantly recognized them as 'kindred spirits' belonging to 'the race that knows Joseph' and became a cherished friend. Later, when John Selwyn's grandson, Owen Ford, visited Four Winds, Captain Jim entrusted him with his manuscript 'life-book.' Owen adapted these real-life adventures into a highly successful novel. Shortly after receiving and reading the published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, his hands resting on his life-book.

label: Appearance
value: Cornelia Bryant is a plump woman.
unit: Cornelia Bryant is a plump, fresh-faced woman with a rosy complexion, jolly brown eyes, and smooth hair coifed or worn with a hard little knob under an old-fashioned sun-hat. Though not given to vanity in her attire, she wears a black dress for church and occasionally dons a calico wrapper with pink rose patterns, or a blue-and-white striped apron, even when making calls. She eventually chooses a navy blue silk dress for her wedding.

label: Personality
value: Cornelia is outspoken.
unit: Outspoken, sharp-tongued, and fiercely opinionated, Cornelia is a staunch Presbyterian with a deep-seated scorn for men, Methodists, and foolishness. Beneath her sarcastic exterior lies an exceptionally kind, generous, and neighborly heart, making her the first to offer practical help to anyone in trouble. She is intensely loyal to her female friends and takes pride in her independence, household skills, and outspoken honesty. Though she insists she despises men, she possesses a keen sense of humor and takes a secret delight in managing them.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years.
unit: Cornelia Bryant lived for many years as an independent spinster in an emerald-green house at Four Winds. Having lost her mother at a young age, she raised her younger brother, whose early death left a lasting mark on her. She maintained a close, protective friendship with Leslie Moore, standing by her through years of hardship. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to the house of dreams at Four Winds, Cornelia quickly bonded with Anne as a 'kindred spirit' of the race that knows Joseph. She actively engaged in church work, served as a leader in the Ladies' Aid Society, and frequently aided destitute families. Though she spent decades scoffing at men and marriage, she eventually agreed to marry her longtime suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he fulfilled his vow to cut his hair and beard upon a Liberal political victory. They married in an intimate ceremony, with Marshall moving into her house at Four Winds.

She maintained a close, protective friendship with Leslie Moore, standing by her through years of hardship. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to the house of dreams at Four Winds, Cornelia quickly bonded with Anne as a 'kindred spirit' of the race that knows Joseph. She actively engaged in church work, served as a leader in the Ladies' Aid Society, and frequently aided destitute families. Though she spent decades scoffing at men and marriage, she eventually agreed to marry her longtime suitor, Marshall Elliott, after he fulfilled his vow to cut his hair and beard upon a Liberal political victory. They married in an intimate ceremony, with Marshall moving into her house at Four Winds.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Dick Moore grew up in Four Winds, working in his father's store during the winters and going to sea in the summers. He became enamored with Leslie West, who repeatedly spurned his advances. Desiring her, Dick manipulated her mother, Rose West, by threatening to have his father foreclose the overdue mortgage on the West farm unless Leslie agreed to marry him. Leslie reluctantly consented in order to save her mother's home, and they were married when she was sixteen. Following her mother's death the next year, Dick left Four Winds on a voyage to Cuba aboard the ship Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died shortly after the ship was forced to leave without him. Because his double cousin, George Moore, stayed behind to nurse him and subsequently suffered an injury that caused total amnesia, George was mistaken for Dick and brought back to Four Winds by Captain Jim, a mistake that remained undiscovered for thirteen years.

label: History
value: Dora's mother died in East Grafton.
unit: Following the death of her mother in East Grafton, Dora and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables. While her brother Davy was constantly getting into trouble, Dora was a model of good behavior, helping Marilla and Anne around the house and keeping her clothes clean. She began attending Avonlea school at seven years old. When her uncle Richard Keith died, he left a trust fund for her and Davy, securing their stay at Green Gables permanently. As she grew into her teens, she inherited the porch gable room at Green Gables after Anne left for college, and eventually began being courted by Ralph Andrews.

While her brother Davy was constantly getting into trouble, Dora was a model of good behavior, helping Marilla and Anne around the house and keeping her clothes clean. She began attending Avonlea school at seven years old. When her uncle Richard Keith died, he left a trust fund for her and Davy, securing their stay at Green Gables permanently. As she grew into her teens, she inherited the porch gable room at Green Gables after Anne left for college, and eventually began being courted by Ralph Andrews.

label: History
value: Gilbert returns to Avonlea School
unit: Gilbert returns to Avonlea School after years in Alberta and immediately becomes Anne Shirley's chief academic rival after jokingly calling her 'Carrots', sparking a long-held grudge. Despite Anne's snubbing, Gilbert repeatedly seeks her friendship and competes closely with her at Queen's Academy. After graduating from Queen's, he teaches at White Sands and surrenders his application for the Avonlea school so Anne can remain near Green Gables. He later attends Redmond College, where he earns High Honors and wins the Cooper Prize in Classics, while also serving as Freshman Class President and captain of the football team. Following a severe bout of typhoid fever, Gilbert reconciles with Anne, and she accepts his proposal of marriage after realizing her true feelings for him. Upon graduating from medical school, Gilbert takes over his great-uncle's practice in Four Winds Harbor, marries Anne in the Green Gables orchard, and settles with her in a small white house on the harbor shore, where they later welcome their son, James Matthew.

He later attends Redmond College, where he earns High Honors and wins the Cooper Prize in Classics, while also serving as Freshman Class President and captain of the football team. Following a severe bout of typhoid fever, Gilbert reconciles with Anne, and she accepts his proposal of marriage after realizing her true feelings for him. value: Mr.
unit: Mr. J. A. Harrison bought the Robert Bell farm in Avonlea, adjoining Green Gables, and moved there as a newcomer. His unconventional housekeeping, erratic meal times, and loud profanity-uttering parrot, Ginger, quickly earned him the reputation of an eccentric crank in the village. Soon after his arrival, he confronted Anne Shirley over her Jersey cow breaking into his oatfield, causing a fiery exchange of insults between them. However, when Anne accidentally sold his cow instead of her own, she went to his house to confess and apologize; Mr. Harrison accepted the mistake graciously, exchanged cows with her, and the two became firm friends. He later joined and supported the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis grew up in Prince Edward Island.
unit: Lavendar Lewis grew up in Prince Edward Island and fell in love as a young woman with Stephen Irving. After a hasty quarrel caused by her pride and flirtatiousness, the engagement was broken and Stephen left for the United States, leaving her heartbroken. Lavendar chose to live a retired, quiet life at Echo Lodge, an ivy-covered stone house in Grafton. To cope with her loneliness, she created a fantasy world of pretend tea parties, echoes, and an imaginary little dream-boy. She employed a series of young maidservants whom she collectively dubbed 'Charlotta.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon Echo Lodge, they quickly became close friends with Lavendar, drawn to her imaginative nature. Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit her, which deeply touched Lavendar. Through Anne's intervention, Stephen Irving returned to visit Lavendar after twenty-five years apart. The two reconciled, realizing their enduring love, and were married in the garden of Echo Lodge under the honeysuckle trellis. Following their wedding, they traveled to the Pacific coast before relocating to Boston, taking Paul and Charlotta the Fourth with them, while keeping Echo Lodge as a beloved summer home.

label: History
value: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island.
unit: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, in a home marked by poverty and affection, but her childhood was shattered at age twelve when she saw her brother Kenneth killed in a wagon accident. Two years later, her idolized father committed suicide, a discovery Leslie made herself. She persevered through her grief, earned her teaching license at Queen's Academy, and taught at the Glen St. Mary school. At age sixteen, she was pressured by her mother into marrying Dick Moore to prevent the foreclosure of their homestead. After her mother died, Dick went to sea and disappeared. Four years later, Captain Jim Boyd found a brain-damaged man in Havana whom he identified as Dick, and brought him back. For eleven years, Leslie selflessly nursed this man—who was mentally a child—while running her farm and taking in occasional summer boarders to survive. Upon meeting her new neighbors, Anne and Gilbert Blythe, Leslie initially struggled with bitter envy of their happy home, but soon formed a profound, soul-deep friendship with Anne. When Gilbert suggested that an operation might restore Dick's mental faculties, Leslie courageously agreed and took him to Montreal, where the surgery succeeded. However, the restored man proved to be Dick's double-cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Suddenly freed from her tragic plight, Leslie returned to Four Winds and eventually admitted her love for Owen Ford, a writer who had boarder with her that summer.

She persevered through her grief, earned her teaching license at Queen's Academy, and taught at the Glen St. Mary school. At age sixteen, she was pressured by her mother into marrying Dick Moore to prevent the foreclosure of their homestead. After her mother died, Dick went to sea and disappeared. Four years later, Captain Jim Boyd found a brain-damaged man in Havana whom he identified as Dick, and brought him back. For eleven years, Leslie selflessly nursed this man—who was mentally a child—while running her farm and taking in occasional summer boarders to survive. Upon meeting her new neighbors, Anne and Gilbert Blythe, Leslie initially struggled with bitter envy of their happy home, but soon formed a profound, soul-deep friendship with Anne. When Gilbert suggested that an operation might restore Dick's mental faculties, Leslie courageously agreed and took him to Montreal, where the surgery succeeded. However, the restored man proved to be Dick's double-cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Suddenly freed from her tragic plight, Leslie returned to Four Winds and eventually admitted her love for Owen Ford, a writer who had boarder with her that summer.

Two years later, her idolized father committed suicide, a discovery Leslie made herself. She persevered through her grief, earned her teaching license at Queen's Academy, and taught at the Glen St. Mary school. At age sixteen, she was pressured by her mother into marrying Dick Moore to prevent the foreclosure of their homestead. After her mother died, Dick went to sea and disappeared. Four years later, Captain Jim Boyd found a brain-damaged man in Havana whom he identified as Dick, and brought him back. For eleven years, Leslie selflessly nursed this man—who was mentally a child—while running her farm and taking in occasional summer boarders to survive. Upon meeting her new neighbors, Anne and Gilbert Blythe, Leslie initially struggled with bitter envy of their happy home, but soon formed a profound, soul-deep friendship with Anne. When Gilbert suggested that an operation might restore Dick's mental faculties, Leslie courageously agreed and took him to Montreal, where the surgery succeeded. However, the restored man proved to be Dick's double-cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Suddenly freed from her tragic plight, Leslie returned to Four Winds and eventually admitted her love for Owen Ford, a writer who had boarder with her that summer.

label: History
value: Little Jem was born at dawn.
unit: Little Jem was born at dawn on a early autumn morning in the little house of dreams at Four Winds Harbor to Anne and Gilbert Blythe. He was named James Matthew after Captain Jim and Matthew Cuthbert, who were regarded as the finest gentlemen his mother had ever known. As a baby, he was doted upon by his parents, as well as Leslie Moore, Susan Baker, Marilla, and Captain Jim, the latter of whom left his curious treasures to the child in his will. When he was about a year old, his parents decided to relocate to the Morgan place at Glen St. Mary, and he moved there with his family.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with her quiet brother Matthew, intending to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm. Through a misunderstanding, an eleven-year-old orphan girl named Anne Shirley was brought to them instead. Though Marilla initially planned to send Anne back, she agreed to keep her at Matthew's urging and took charge of her upbringing. Over the years, Marilla raised Anne with firm discipline, guiding her through school scrapes and growing deeply attached to her. When her eyes began failing and Matthew died suddenly, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally so Marilla would not have to sell the farm. Later, when Anne decided to attend Redmond College after all, Marilla arranged for her widowed neighbor, Mrs. Rachel Lynde, to move into Green Gables so they could keep house together and raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. Marilla welcomed Anne back during college vacations, helped prepare for her wedding to Gilbert Blythe in the Green Gables orchard, and continued living at Green Gables with Mrs. Lynde and the twins.

label: History
value: During a bitter political campaign fifteen years before the Liberals came to power, Marshall Elliott vowed publicly at a meeting.
unit: During a particularly bitter political campaign fifteen years before the Liberals came to power, Marshall Elliott vowed publicly at a meeting that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Grit party was elected. Because the Liberals remained out of power for years, he grew an extraordinarily long beard and mane of hair, making him a well-known eccentric in the area. When the Liberals finally won a general election years later, he immediately went to the Glen St. Mary barber at midnight and had his hair cut and beard shaved off. Shortly afterwards, he married Miss Cornelia Bryant and moved to her farm to live.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables with his sister Marilla. Due to advancing age and heart trouble, the siblings decide to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm work, but a misunderstanding results in the arrival of an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley. Matthew is instantly won over by Anne's cheerful chatter on the drive from the station and quietly insists on keeping her. Over the next four years, he remains Anne's devoted confidant and champion, frequently spoiling her with treats and a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas. When Anne passes her entrance examinations to Queen's Academy and subsequently wins the Avery Scholarship, Matthew takes immense pride in her achievements. Following her graduation, Matthew suffers a sudden, fatal heart attack upon reading news of the failure of the Abbey Bank, where his life savings were deposited, and he is buried in the Avonlea graveyard.

label: History
value: Owen Ford was born in Ontario.
unit: Owen Ford was born in Ontario, the son of Alice Selwyn and grandson of John Selwyn, the first schoolmaster of Glen St. Mary who built the little house of dreams. After working for years as a journalist and magazine writer, he suffered a severe bout of typhoid fever and was ordered to the seaside by his doctor to recuperate. In August, he went to Four Winds, boarders' accommodations having been arranged for him by Miss Cornelia Bryant at the home of Leslie Moore. Upon his arrival, Owen was struck by Leslie's extraordinary beauty, and soon fell deeply in love with her. Learning that her husband, Dick Moore, was hopelessly brain-damaged, Owen hid his feelings and poured his creative energies into writing a novel based on the 'life-book' of Captain Jim Boyd. After completing the manuscript in late summer, Owen confessed his agonizing, secret love for Leslie to Anne Blythe, before departing for Toronto without revealing his feelings to Leslie herself. Later, after Gilbert Blythe's medical intervention restored the memory of the man believed to be Dick Moore—revealing him to be his cousin, George Moore—Leslie became a free woman. Upon learning the news, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, and they became engaged to be married in December. He also purchased the little house of dreams from the church trustees to serve as their summer home.

unit: Owen Ford was born in Ontario, the son of Alice Selwyn and grandson of John Selwyn, the first schoolmaster of Glen St. Mary who built the little house of dreams. After working for years as a journalist and magazine writer, he suffered a severe bout of typhoid fever and was ordered to the seaside by his doctor to recuperate. In August, he went to Four Winds, boarders' accommodations having been arranged for him by Miss Cornelia Bryant at the home of Leslie Moore. Upon his arrival, Owen was struck by Leslie's extraordinary beauty, and soon fell deeply in love with her. Learning that her husband, Dick Moore, was hopelessly brain-damaged, Owen hid his feelings and poured his creative energies into writing a novel based on the 'life-book' of Captain Jim Boyd. After completing the manuscript in late summer, Owen confessed his agonizing, secret love for Leslie to Anne Blythe, before departing for Toronto without revealing his feelings to Leslie herself. Later, after Gilbert Blythe's medical intervention restored the memory of the man believed to be Dick Moore—revealing him to be his cousin, George Moore—Leslie became a free woman. Upon learning the news, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, and they became engaged to be married in December. He also purchased the little house of dreams from the church trustees to serve as their summer home.

value: Paul has a delicate face.
unit: Paul has a delicate, refined, and exceptionally beautiful face framed in a halo of chestnut curls, which he later crops short as he grows older. He has big, dark blue eyes that match his father's, and an expressive, crimson-lipped mouth with a dimpled corner. Though small for his age during his early years in Avonlea, he eventually shoots up into a tall, handsome, and sturdy youth.

value: Paul is a highly imaginative boy.
unit: Paul is a highly imaginative, sensitive, and meditative boy who possesses a rare poetic soul and a deep appreciation for beauty. Though thoughtful, grave, and given to vivid daydreams about 'rock people' and fairies, he is also manly, good-tempered, and well-liked by his peers in school games. He is deeply affectionate and loyal, holding a reverent devotion to his late mother and a strong sense of duty toward his family.

unit: Paul is a highly imaginative, sensitive, and meditative boy who possesses a rare poetic soul and a deep appreciation for beauty. label: History
value: Paul Irving was born in the United States.
unit: Paul Irving was born in the United States to Stephen Irving and his wife, who died when Paul was a small child. At ten years old, he was sent to Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving. He enrolled in Avonlea School, where he quickly formed an intense bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, recognizing her as a kindred spirit who understood his rich imaginary world of 'rock people.' When his father visited Avonlea, Paul helped reunite Stephen with his old love, Miss Lavendar Lewis, whom Paul warmly accepted as a second mother. Paul later moved to Boston with his father, Miss Lavendar, and Charlotta the Fourth. Over the years, he maintained a faithful correspondence with Anne and developed a talent for poetry, eventually publishing verses. At sixteen, he returned to the Island for a summer visit before going abroad to Europe for two years of study, attending Anne and Gilbert's wedding at Green Gables.

value: Philippa is gay
unit: Philippa is gay, irrepressible, and intensely charming, possessing a whimsical and volatile nature. Though she appears shallow, frivolous, and indecisive on the surface, she is fiercely loyal, generous, and has a deep, womanly heart. She is candidly aware of her own beauty and popularity, enjoying the admiration of many suitors without malice. Despite her luxurious upbringing, she is cheerful and willing to adapt to a simpler, poorer lifestyle for the sake of true love.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he notoriously paid more attention to his grown-up sixteen-year-old student, Prissy Andrews, than to his educational duties. During his tenure, he humiliated Anne Shirley on several occasions, such as holding up her slate with spelling errors, forcing her to stand on the platform under a blackboard inscription mocking her temper after she broke her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and making her sit beside Gilbert as a punishment for being late. Following a period of stubborn resistance, Anne refused to attend his school for weeks until he unfairly punished her again. During the winter, he took part in the Avonlea Debating Club's grand concert by reciting Mark Antony's oration over the body of Caesar. At the end of June, his engagement at Avonlea school ended, and he gave an affecting farewell speech to his pupils before leaving the settlement permanently.

A loyal and affectionate chum, she shares a deep bond of friendship with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. She is deeply appreciative of the beauty in nature and poetry, yet remains sensible and grounded.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley, after which she taught school at Carmody for a time. She resigned her post to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, joining Anne, Gilbert Blythe, and Charlie Sloane. During her first year at Redmond, she lived in a St. John Street boardinghouse with Anne and quickly struck up a close friendship with Philippa Gordon. In their Sophomore year, Priscilla, Anne, Philippa, and Stella Maynard rented Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, keeping house together under the chaperonage of Stella's Aunt Jamesina. Priscilla pursued a course in Classics, eventually graduating with Honors. Following her time at Redmond, she went to Japan.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken woman
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken, capable, and formidable woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly industrious and managing, she involves herself deeply in both her own affairs and those of her neighbors. Though she can be blunt, opinionated, and sharp-tongued, she possesses a warm, kind heart and is always among the first to offer practical help to those in need. She holds strong religious and political convictions, remaining a devout Presbyterian and an ardent Liberal.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: Jonas Blake studied theology at St. Columbia and served at the Prospect Point Mission Church during his college years. label: History
value: Roy Gardner entered Redmond College.
unit: Roy Gardner entered Redmond College, but interrupted his studies after his Sophomore year to accompany his mother abroad for her health. Returning to Redmond after two years, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a autumn rainstorm when her umbrella turned inside out, rescuing her with his own umbrella. He began courting her attentively, sending her flowers and verse, and bringing her into his social circle. During Anne's Senior year, Roy proposed to her at the harbor pavilion in Kingsport, but she rejected his proposal upon realizing she did not truly love him. Heartbroken, he left Kingsport, but later recovered and married another woman, settling down into a happy life.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy, she earned a teacher's license and took a teaching position at Carmody School. Known for her beauty and flirtatious nature, she pursued a lively social life surrounded by suitors. However, after contracting a severe lung congestion, she developed galloping consumption and was forced to give up teaching. Throughout her illness, Ruby maintained a facade of recovery and spoke constantly of her future plans, but privately suffered great dread of dying young. Shortly before her death, she reconciled an old feud with her childhood friend Emma White and confessed her fears and heartaches to Anne. Ruby passed away peacefully in her sleep at the age of seventeen, leaving a lasting impression of her beauty upon the Avonlea community.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the first female schoolteacher in Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the first female schoolteacher in Avonlea, succeeding Mr. Phillips. She quickly wins the devotion of her pupils, including Anne Shirley, by introducing innovative educational methods such as nature field afternoons, physical culture exercises, and Friday recitation sessions. In November, she organizes a successful student concert to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Recognizing the potential of her advanced pupils, she forms an extra after-school class to prepare them for the Queen's Academy Entrance examinations. Although offered a teaching position in her home district, she declines it in order to remain in Avonlea and see her students through their final preparations. Under her guidance, her pupils make great progress, culminating in Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe tying for first place on the Island. After two years of teaching in Avonlea, Miss Stacy leaves for a new position and eventually marries in California.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant before taking up a country schoolteaching post for two years. Growing weary of the trials and misunderstandings of country teaching, she decided to resume her studies at Redmond College, entering directly as a Sophomore. Tired of boardinghouse life, Stella proposed that she, Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon rent a house together—Patty's Place—with her Aunt Jamesina acting as housekeeper. During her time at Redmond, she actively participated in college life, wrote papers for the Philomathic Society, and successfully completed her Arts degree.

Growing weary of the trials and misunderstandings of country teaching, she decided to resume her studies at Redmond College, entering directly as a Sophomore. Tired of boardinghouse life, Stella proposed that she, Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon rent a house together—Patty's Place—with her Aunt Jamesina acting as housekeeper. During her time at Redmond, she actively participated in college life, wrote papers for the Philomathic Society, and successfully completed her Arts degree.

label: History
value: Susan Baker is a spinster
unit: Susan Baker, a spinster from Glen St. Mary, was hired to assist Anne Blythe at her house of dreams during Anne's illness and the birth of her first child. She quickly became an indispensable member of the household, taking complete charge of domestic affairs and forming a deep, protective devotion to 'young Mrs. Doctor' and her family. She stayed on permanently through the summer and winter, caring for Little Jem with fierce affection. After briefly leaving to nurse her sister Matilda, who had broken a leg, Susan returned to the little house and eventually moved with the Blythes when they relocated to their new home at the Glen.
